To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximal inotropy induced by ET-1 is augmented by inhibition of NOS, whereas that of AM is not, and that the inotropy induced in combination by AM and ET- 1 is suppressed by endogenous myocardial NO.

the inotropic response of the isolated rat heart to ET-1 and AM is potentiated by NOS inhibition and that the inotropic effect of combined administration of low, submaximal doses of ET-1 and of AM is depressed by endogenous NO.

inhibition of myocardial NO synthesis enhances the inotropic effect of ET-1 but has only a minor effect on the response to AM; meanwhile, the inotropic response of combined administration of low, submaximal doses of AM and endothelin-1 is substantially inhibited by endogenous NO.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of myocardially generated NO on the inotropic responses to ET-1 and AM.
a novel mechanism for the regulation of cardiac inotropy by NO, which may be of relevance for the therapeutic use of cardioactive peptides.
the impact of myocardially generated nitric oxide on the inotropic responses to the cardioactive peptides endothelin-1 and adrenomedulin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
myocardial NO synthesis is involved in the regulation of the inotropic effects of AM and ET1, although the impact is not identical.
NO exerts a differential impact on inotropic response to the two peptides, which is in part dependent upon peptide concentration.
the impact of endogenous NO on the inotropic effects of AM and ET is dose-dependent and that it can be overcome by inhibition of myocardium NOS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NO is a potent modulator of the inotropic effects of ET-1 and AM in the isolated perfused heart preparation.
the inotropic response of the myocardium to AM is less dependent on endogenous NO synthesis than the response to ET- 1.
NO has an impact on inotropic responses of the heart, and that the impact depends on the nature of the stimulus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of NO on the inotropic action of cardioactive peptides may be dependent on the peptide and the dose of the peptide.

myocardial NO synthesis is not involved in mediating the inotropic effects of AM, but it can significantly enhance the inotropic response of ET-1 at high concentrations, and can suppress the inotropic response induced by combined administration of low concentrations of ET-1 and AM.
NO has a different impact on the inotropic effects of ET-1 and AM.
